description: You already know your waist-to-height number. This episode is about using it: the ratio as a weekly compass that tells you whether your recomp is actually working, which direction to adjust, and why the trend matters more than any single morning's decimal.

beats.text: A TREND YOU CAN STEER BY

scenes.narration: You may have taken this test before; today we take it like navigators. Same ritual: waist at the belly button, relaxed, breathing out, first thing in the morning, after the bathroom, before food or drink. Height once, honestly, it never changes. Divide, and write the decimal down with today's date beside it, in a notebook or a phone note you will actually keep, because today's test is not the decimal itself. It is the start of a line. A single waist-to-height reading tells you where you stand; four Monday readings tell you where you are going, and direction, in a recomp, is worth more than position. The scale gives you a number every day and a story that changes with the weather. This ratio, taken weekly under identical conditions, gives you something rarer: a trend you can steer by. Got today's decimal, dated and written? Keep it. At the end I will show you how to read the line it begins, including the week the number goes the wrong way, which is coming, and which means less than you fear.

scenes.label: THE LINE, AND THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE
scenes.narration: The line is still 0.5, waist under half of height, and if you need the full story of that number, it lives in the belly episode. Today the line gets a second dimension: speed. On an honest recomp, a skinny fat man should expect the ratio to fall by roughly a hundredth a month, about a centimeter or two of waist per month at average height, while his weight barely moves. That sounds slow until you compound it: six months at that pace is the entire borderland crossed, belly to athletic, without a single week of dieting misery. Slower than that for two straight months, with training, protein and sleep honestly in place, is the signal to adjust exactly one variable, steps, protein or the deficit, never all three. Faster than that usually means muscle is leaving with the fat, the crash pattern wearing a compass costume. So the number now has a speedometer. Hold your decimal and your expected pace against the line.
scenes.sub: trend down 0.01 a month: the recomp is working - frozen 2 months: adjust one signal

lines: The waist reports the deep fat.
beats.title: FIXED ANCHOR, HONEST SIGNAL

beats.text: A HUNDREDTH MEANS MORE THAN 2 KILOS

scenes.narration: Here is why navigators trust this instrument above the scale: the ratio is trade-proof. A recomp is an exchange, fat out, muscle in, and nearly every common measure gets confused by the exchange. Weight cannot see it at all. Body-fat scales guess at it through wet feet and wishful algorithms. Even the mirror struggles in the early weeks, when the changes are real but sub-visual. The waist-to-height ratio cuts through because its two parts are chosen perfectly: the waist is the one circumference that falls when deep fat leaves, and height is the one measurement that never moves, never fluctuates with water, salt, glycogen or mood. Every other instrument you own has a moving denominator or a noisy numerator. This one has a fixed anchor and an honest signal, which is why a hundredth of movement here means more than two kilos on the scale. When men say the recomp feels invisible for the first month, they are usually watching instruments that cannot see it. This one can, from week two, if you let it accumulate Mondays.

beats.text: READ THE LINE, NOT THE READINGS

lines: A bad morning is a wave.
beats.title: WAVES VS THE TIDE

scenes.narration: Now learn to read the compass through bad weather, because the waist has noise of its own and panicking at noise is how good recomp plans die. A salty restaurant meal, a poor night, a hard leg session two days ago, even a large glass of water at the wrong moment can each add a visible centimeter on a given morning, and a centimeter at average height is nearly a hundredth of ratio, your entire month of progress, apparently erased by Tuesday's dinner. This is why the protocol is weekly and the judgment is monthly: you are not reading readings, you are reading the line through the readings, the way a navigator reads a course through waves. Four Mondays, plot them honestly, and ask only one question: is the line, through all its wobbling, tilted down? If yes, the answer to every individual bad morning is the same: nothing is wrong, change nothing, take next Monday's reading. The men who fail recomp rarely fail at training or eating.

There is one more reading skill, and it is the difference between a compass and a crystal ball: knowing what a frozen ratio is trying to say. When the decimal refuses to move for two months despite honest training, the cause is almost never mysterious, and it is almost never your metabolism. Run the audit in the order this season taught you. Protein first, because it is the most commonly faked, estimated generously and eaten rarely. Steps second, because the 5,000-step life quietly cancels good training. Sleep third, because five-hour nights keep the stress signals aimed at the waist no matter what the days do. And only then the deficit itself, which may simply be zero, a man eating exactly at maintenance while expecting storage to shrink out of politeness. The compass does not fix the ship. It tells you, with unusual honesty, that the ship is not moving, and the checklist tells you which of four ropes is holding it. One adjustment, one month, one new line of Mondays.

beats.label: OF KEPT PROMISES CHANGE THE MAN

scenes.narration: Now the advantage of navigating this way, and it is psychological as much as physical. The scale-watcher lives in a casino: daily numbers, daily emotions, a plan rewritten by every fluctuation, and a quit rate to match. The compass man lives in a laboratory: one reading a week, one judgment a month, one variable changed at a time, and a growing page of decimals that prove, in his own handwriting, that his body obeys cause and effect. For a skinny fat man this calm is not a luxury; it is the mechanism of success itself, because recomp is a six-month project and only calm men finish six-month projects. There is a compounding dignity in it too. Each Monday's decimal is a small kept promise, and a man with twenty kept promises stops identifying as someone who fails at this. The belly shrinks almost as a side effect of becoming the kind of person whose ship has a compass and a course. You already took the hardest step: you measured honestly. Navigation is just refusing to un-measure yourself with panic.
Now brace with me. Dead bug holds: back pressed to the floor, opposite arm and leg reaching long, exhale as you extend. The waist learns its new job. Go.

Here is the navigation protocol, complete. Every Monday: the ritual measurement, the decimal written and dated, no commentary, no mood attached. Every month: one honest look at the line, tilted down, flat, or up, and at most one adjustment from the checklist, chosen in order. Every quarter: the photo protocol from the mirror episode, because the compass tracks the waist and the camera audits everything else. Now the mistakes, all of them interpretation errors. Measuring at random times and comparing unlike with unlike. Adjusting three variables after one flat month, which destroys the experiment and teaches you nothing. And the subtlest: secretly switching the goal when the ratio moves slowly, from recomp to aggressive cut, then wondering why the muscle and the morale leave together. A compass is only useful to a man who has chosen a destination. Yours is under 0.5 with muscle rising, and the course, give or take a hundredth a month, is already drawn.

beats.text: A VERDICT BECAME A LINE TODAY

beats.label: THE NEXT POINT ON THE LINE

lines: Steer the line, keep the pace.
beats.title: YOUR VERDICT

scenes.narration: So, your decimal, read as a navigator reads it. Under 0.5 and holding: you are in safe waters, and the project is muscle, with the compass standing guard against creep. Between 0.5 and 0.55: you are on the course this episode drew, and your only job is pace-keeping, a hundredth a month, judged in Mondays. Above 0.55: the course is longer but identically drawn, and the first months often move fastest as the deep fat, the eager fat, begins to leave. And if your line has been frozen: do not curse the compass for the reading, run the four-rope checklist and cut exactly one rope. Whatever today's decimal is, it now has a date beside it, which means it has already stopped being a verdict and become the first point of a line. Lines can be steered. Put your number in the comments, just the decimal and, if you have them, last month's too. We plot the next point in thirty days.

Same tape, same Monday ritual, thirty days from now: that is the retest. If this way of training makes sense to you, subscribe, because we test a new signal every episode. This is {channel}. Train the cable.
